issues.reason: *Names and casing* prescribes the opposite of what the reviewer cites — it forbids a MODIFIER genus on a name (kestrel_river is not kestrel) while requiring the entity's kind 'in one ordinary type atom ... whether the kind word sits inside the name or beside it' ('the Kestrel River' -> (Member kestrel_river river)) — and (Member quartet group) is true and well-typed.

The preposition-named oblique's 'object NP follows the ordinary NP rules (an article mints a witness with its kind atom)' (*Thematic roles*), so 'on the question of whether P' must mint sk_question_1 with its typing and carry the Whether term as the noun's own argument, not substitute the sealed term for the NP.

*Compound concepts* makes fusion determined, not optional, for an adjective+noun pair naming a recognized kind and names the nationality/origin adjective as a fusing case (breton_tapestry), so 'the Palestinian people' is palestinian_people plus its genus atoms, not a split kind + property.

*Partitives* cues the count route off a plural 'the Ns' and the mass/heterogeneous route off a singular 'the N'; 'the Quartet' is a singular collective whose member kind the text never states, so (GroupOf sk_rest_1 <kind>) would have to invent one — and PartOf is also the licensed group-member head (*Coordination & plurals*).

gaps_confirmed: a split-ratio adverbial ('divided three-to-one') — no licensed encoding for the ratio itself
a verbless absolute phrase naming the sides of a split ('the United States against the rest')
a question-denoting noun taking an embedded question as its complement ('the question of whether P') — *Embedded questions* covers only a verb's sealed Theme
new_gaps: a proper name whose only kind word IS the name ('the Quartet') — the required type atom has no distinct kind lemma to use, forcing either a circular (Member quartet quartet) or a generalization
a predicative participle that is stative-adjectival rather than verbal ('is divided three-to-one') — the inflection/derivation rule decides by function but gives no test for a resultant-state passive
